# Automatic texture atlas

@difference Extension: small textures that are loaded from files are merged into shared images by the runtime, so that scenes with many of them need fewer draw calls; [TextureAtlas](TextureAtlas) turns it off.

The 3D renderer draws everything that has the same mesh, texture and state in one call, and each different texture breaks that. When a program loads many small textures (sprites, icons, particles), BlitzLLVM copies them into pages of 1024 by 1024 pixels at the next [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) and gives every texture a view of its rectangle, the same as [AtlasTexture](AtlasTexture) makes.

A sampler of a graphics card can neither wrap nor go down the mip levels inside a rectangle of an image, so the fragment shader reads views itself: it takes the four texels it needs from the two levels of detail that are closest, wraps their numbers inside the rectangle (repeat, mirror, clamp or border color, as the flags or the [sampler](CreateSampler) of the texture say) and mixes them by hand. The mip levels of the picture are copied to the same levels of the page, with the picture placed where they line up. So repeating, mirrored and mip mapped textures are merged too, and coordinates outside 0 to 1 never show a neighbour. The result is the same as without the merging up to the rounding of a sampler (a step in a channel), and where nearest mip levels switch. Anisotropic filtering of a [sampler](SetSamplerAnisotropy) is not done for views.

Only textures that this cannot change are merged: loaded from a file, at most 256 by 256 pixels, 8 bits per channel, and not a sphere or cube map, render target, sheet of frames, atlas, compressed or sRGB texture. [ScaleTexture](ScaleTexture), [PositionTexture](PositionTexture), [RotateTexture](RotateTexture) and [SetTextureSampler](SetTextureSampler) work on merged textures as they do on others. [TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer) needs a picture of its own, so a merged texture gets one back when it is used, and is not merged again. The rectangles of freed textures are not reused; a page is freed with its last texture. Merging costs a copy on the graphics card for every texture, which adds a little to loading, and a view costs a little more in the fragment shader than a plain texture does.
